newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Bull trend in T-bonds looking tired.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bull trend in T-bonds looking tired.

text.p: Treasury bond futures have run smack into a troubling resistance level and could be poised for a pullback of a point or more, technical analysts said Thursday.
"It's starting to be an area where I think it's prone to establish a fairly significant long-term top," said Gerry DeMers, technical analyst for Fuji Securities Inc.
September bond futures' steep incline since April culminated in a new 1-1/2-year high at 115-23/32 Wednesday. The contract was last trading down 8/32 at 115-04/32.
"The trend right now is at a critical juncture," said David Lundgren, senior analyst at Technical Data.
Bond futures gapped higher on Wednesday's open, set the new high, then retreated to settle near where they began, forming a bearish "shooting star" on single candlestick charts, Lundgren said.
Confirmation of the bearish candlestick pattern today would indicate the uptrend had stalled and the contract could backpedal toward the mid- to low 114-00 handle, Lundgren said.

The analyst said he was also monitoring a pair of trend trackers that suggest the bull market could be faltering. Moving average convergence/divergence is wavering, he said, while a "trend intensity" proprietary indicator has stalled at relatively extended levels.
Meanwhile, daily and weekly stochastics have been signaling the market's overbought status since September bonds climbed above 112-00, Lundgren noted.

In Elliott Wave analysis, 115-22/32 represents significant long-term resistance as an A-B-C target, said Fuji's DeMers. It also represents the 61.8 percent retracement of the downmove from about 122-00 to 105-00, he said.
Though the relentless rally has conditioned market participants to buy dips, the importance of this resistance area is beginning to loom large, he said.
"I think the next major move is down," said DeMers.
One bond floor analyst said that although the market was clinging to the bullish scenario, a retreat to the high 113-00s or low 114-00s was a distinct possibility.
"When the market goes up this steeply, you have farther to fall," he said.
